title: Dimension shifting for Tor along a free presentation
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $0\to K\xrightarrow{j}F\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules with $F$ a free $R$-module, and $N$ an $R$-module. Then for every integer $i\ge1$ there is an isomorphism of $R$-modules $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,N)$, with $\operatorname{Tor}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. In particular $\operatorname{Tor}^R_2(M,N)=0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(K,N)=0$.

proof.text: A free resolution of $K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split] to the short exact sequence $0\to K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_K}K\to0\to0$ ($\mathrm{id}_K$ injective, $\ker(K\to0)=K=\operatorname{im}\mathrm{id}_K$, $K\to0$ surjective) and keep only its first resolution: this gives a chain complex $G_\bullet$ ($n\ge0$, differentials $e_n:G_n\to G_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$) of free $R$-modules with an $R$-linear augmentation $\eta:G_0\to K$ such that $\cdots\to G_2\xrightarrow{e_2}G_1\xrightarrow{e_1}G_0\xrightarrow{\eta}K\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (section-tor, lines 18215--18236): 'Choose a resolution $F_\bullet$ of $M$ by free $R$-modules'

proof.text: Splicing. Define $F'_0=F$ and $F'_{n+1}=G_n$ for $n\ge0$, with differentials $d'_1=j\circ\eta:G_0\to F$ and $d'_{n+1}=e_n:G_n\to G_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$, and augmentation $p:F'_0=F\to M$. All $F'_n$ are free ($F$ by hypothesis, $G_n$ by Step 1) [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The augmented complex $\cdots\to F'_2\xrightarrow{d'_2}F'_1\xrightarrow{d'_1}F'_0\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: $p$ is surjective; $pd'_1=pj\eta=0$ and $\operatorname{im}d'_1=j(\eta(G_0))=j(K)=\ker p$ because $\eta$ is surjective and the given sequence is exact; $d'_1d'_2=j\eta e_1=0$ and $\ker d'_1=\ker(j\eta)=\ker\eta=\operatorname{im}e_1=\operatorname{im}d'_2$ because $j$ is injective; for $n\ge2$, $d'_n d'_{n+1}=e_{n-1}e_n=0$ and $\ker d'_n=\ker e_{n-1}=\operatorname{im}e_n=\operatorname{im}d'_{n+1}$ by exactness of Step 1. So $(F'_\bullet,p)$ is a free resolution of $M$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), lines 35476--35477 ('Since $N^0$ is free, we also see that $\text{Tor}_2^B(H^0, C) = \text{Tor}_1^B(M, C)$'), stated there without proof; argument written by the agent

proof.text: Comparison in degrees $\ge2$. Free modules are allowed as the projective resolutions of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], so by that definition (independence of the resolution up to canonical isomorphism) $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,N)\cong H_{i+1}(F'_\bullet\otimes_RN)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,N)\cong H_i(G_\bullet\otimes_RN)$, as $R$-modules. Let $i\ge1$. In $F'_\bullet\otimes_RN$ the part around degree $i+1$ is $F'_{i+2}\otimes N\xrightarrow{d'_{i+2}\otimes1}F'_{i+1}\otimes N\xrightarrow{d'_{i+1}\otimes1}F'_i\otimes N$; since $i+1\ge2$ and $i+2\ge2$, Step 2 gives $d'_{i+2}=e_{i+1}$, $d'_{i+1}=e_i$ and $F'_{i+2}=G_{i+1}$, $F'_{i+1}=G_i$, $F'_i=G_{i-1}$, so this is literally $G_{i+1}\otimes N\xrightarrow{e_{i+1}\otimes1}G_i\otimes N\xrightarrow{e_i\otimes1}G_{i-1}\otimes N$, the part of $G_\bullet\otimes_RN$ around degree $i$. Hence $H_{i+1}(F'_\bullet\otimes N)=\ker(e_i\otimes1)/\operatorname{im}(e_{i+1}\otimes1)=H_i(G_\bullet\otimes N)$, and composing, $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,N)$ as $R$-modules. (For $i=0$ the argument fails since $d'_1=j\eta\neq e_0$; this is why the statement requires $i\ge1$.) The case $i=1$ gives $\operatorname{Tor}^R_2(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(K,N)$, so one is $0$ iff the other is.
